title: Modified Common Fungal DNA Extraction Buffer (XNA)
author: Stephen D Douglas Russell

steps.title: Prepare Modified Common Fungal DNA Extraction Buffer (XNA)
steps.instruction: Prepare the XNA buffer by combining reagents in a bottle and adjusting the pH.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 mL of 1 M Tris Buffer pH 8.0 using a sterile, DNA-free 50 mL conical tube.
Add 9.3 g of KCl (ACS or Reagent Grade) and dissolve by swirling the closed bottle.
Add 1 M NaOH starting with 10 mL, then adding 1 mL at a time until the pH is between 9 and 9.5 (measured via pH paper or pH meter).
Top up the final solution to 500 mL total volume using molecular grade water.

steps.title: Sterilize and Store XNA Buffer
steps.instruction: Sterilize the prepared XNA buffer and store it under appropriate conditions.

substeps.instruction: Filter sterilize using a DNAse-free 0.22 micron vacuum filter (or syringe filters).
Store in 50 mL tubes at 4 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Prepare DNA Dilution Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare a buffer for diluting raw DNA extracts.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 mL DNA grade 1 M Tris buffer pH 8.0 to a clean 1 L vessel.
Add 200 µL 0.5 M EDTA using a p200 or p1000 pipette with sterile, filtered tips.

In a laminar flow cabinet or clean space, add approximately 350 mL of molecular-grade water into a clean vessel (e.g., acid-washed and autoclaved glass flask or a bottle opened only in a laminar flow cabinet) capable of holding 500 mL with volume gradations.
If prepared outside of a laminar flow cabinet or using non-sterile reagents, filter sterilize using a 0.22 micron vacuum filter.
Transfer the final solution into sterile 50 mL tubes.

steps.title: Extract DNA from Tissue
steps.instruction: Perform DNA extraction from tissue samples using the XNA buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL of extraction buffer to a standard PCR tube.
Add a very small amount of tissue to the buffer (note: 1 mg is often too much for this volume), or add tissue first and then the buffer.
Allow to sit at room temperature for at least 10 minutes (macerating or disrupting tissue is optimal but not necessary).
Heat the PCR tube in a thermal cycler at 95 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Dilute and Store DNA Extracts
steps.instruction: Dilute the raw DNA extracts using the prepared dilution buffer.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the raw DNA extract to the preferred concentration (a standard dilution is 1:10).
Use the diluted DNA immediately or store at -20 °C.
